jobs.title: Security Specialist/HARPS Guard I - PT On Call Floater hours
jobs.description:
Position: PART-TIME PT Floater hours


SCHEDULE: on-call floater hours


Specific Tasks. The following tasks are general duties for the HARPS personnel. Contracting Personnel (CP) providing service at JBSA-Lackland and Randolph, AFB shall perform the following tasks below;

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS: • Monitor all electromagnetic door locks, door contact switches, duress alarms and answer all telephone calls within the HARPS/Information Desk Control Area. This area is defined as the Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) room, and the adjacent administrative area commonly referred to as the Information Desk. • Personnel will monitor the Identipass, Genetech, and Premisys access control systems. • Initial training for these systems will be provided by a company representative of which the system is being provided by. The contractor will then be responsible to train any new CP thereafter. • The government will phase out any of the systems that will eventually no longer be in use. • Operate, observe and evaluate CCTVs within the HARPS/Information Desk Control Area. • Use the Government provided radio system to notify the Facility Management staff and/or the base installation Security Forces on any alarm or police response situations. • Monitor operations and status of overall security network for the MTF from the centralized console. • Operate HARPS/Information Desk intercom system master station at the console to communicate with entry/exit points or incident locations. • Utilize overhead paging system to notify personnel of emergency codes and alarms. Communicate all information in a clear and concise manner. • Operate video recorder and playback at the request of Facility Management personnel. • Maintain security log and activate control devices for interior and exterior doors. • Receive transfer calls from designated wing agencies and take messages or forward calls to appropriate agencies. • Report and initiate an action report log on any emergency situation and provide comprehensive information to responding agencies and Facility Management staff when appropriate. • Maintain up to date roster of on-call and emergency contact personnel for required areas. • The CP report to an appropriate authority (DCS Supervisors, Security Forces, and Facility Managers) any information or circumstances, which may pose a threat to the security of DoD personnel, contractor personnel, resources, and classified or unclassified defense information. • Maintain Chronology of Events, Access Control logs and Alarm Reports at all times. Event logs will be documented in a professional manner utilizing appropriate grammar and punctuation and include all pertinent information covering the parameters of “Who, What, When, and Where.” Event logs will be sent to Facility Management on a daily basis no later than 0800 hrs. These documents are for official use only. • CP shall perform and document physical checks of assigned buildings, rooms and areas when electronic systems are degraded. This includes manual fire watch procedures when fire alarm systems are down and checks of controlled areas such as pharmacies when Intrution Detection Systems (IDS) are degraded. • Act as the information focal point for all medical groups' personnel, patients and visitors on all resource protection activities and the liaison on these issues to the facility management office.


Qualifications.

  1. Have 12 months of experience as an alarm monitor or dispatcher, either in the military or civilian sector, within the last 3 years.
  2. Skills and Knowledge. Must be able to use, at minimum, Access Control System, Genetech, and Microsoft Programs such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  3. Shall be capable of sitting for an extended period of time during the course of their 8-hour shift, but are able to get up and move about within the area. CP shall be capable of bending, reaching, and lifting a minimum of 30 pounds to move and retrieve records or equipment, and may require prolonged walking and or standing.
  4. Personnel must be able to communicate in a clear and concise manner and demonstrate a calm demeanor during high-stress situations

jobs.title: Basic Security Fundamental Support Instructor II (Swim Tester / Lifeguard)
jobs.description:
Type: Full Time

Location: NTTC Lackland/ San Antonio, Texas

Overtime Exempt: No

Reports To: ARMADA HQ

Duties & Responsibilities

  • The Basic Security Fundamental Support Instructor II (Swim Tester / Lifeguard) administers Navy Second Class Swimmer testing for designated Master‑at‑Arms students in accordance with NETC P1552/16 swim testing standards.
  • The Basic Security Fundamental Support Instructor II (Swim Tester / Lifeguard) conducts all poolside safety checks, verify facility readiness, ensure required safety equipment is present, and confirm communication capabilities.
  • Perform lifeguard duties during all swim testing events and evaluate students in accordance with Navy Swimming and Water Survival Instructor Manual guidelines.
  • Complete the Record of Swim Qualification and ensure accurate documentation of all results.
  • Coordinate with NTTC Lackland administrative staff to record successful or unsuccessful test completions in FLTMPS and in student service records.
  • Assist with scheduling pool access and work directly with NTTC and Joint Base San Antonio swimming facility personnel.
  • Deliver CPR instruction and support other non‑weapons training modules within MA "A" School after obtaining CUIT qualifications.
  • Ensure compliance with medical pre‑screening requirements, swimmer safety policies, and high‑risk training precautions.
  • The Basic Security Fundamental Support Instructor II (Swim Tester / Lifeguard) maintains all required certifications and ensures documentation is properly filed in the Instructor Training Jacket (ITJ).
  • Other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities (KSAs)

  • Knowledge of Navy swim testing procedures, water survival standards, and CPR instruction requirements.
  • Ability to perform lifeguard duties, administer swim qualifications, and evaluate student safety and performance.
  • Strong understanding of aquatic safety practices, rescue procedures, and emergency response techniques.
  • Ability to coordinate with medical, administrative, and facility personnel to ensure compliance with screening, documentation, and reporting processes.
  • Strong communication skills for delivering CPR instruction and supporting training modules.
  • Ability to maintain physical readiness to perform water‑based rescue, testing, and instructional tasks.

Minimum/General Experience

  • Possess current certification as a lifeguard. Lifeguard certification requires one of the following:
    • American Red Cross Lifeguard Training
    • YMCA Lifeguard Training
    • Ellis and Associates Water Park Training
    • Possession of one of the following military qualifications:
      • Navy NEC 801A (Navy Rescue Swimmer – Surface)
      • Navy NEC O26A (Special Warfare Operator (SEAL))
      • Navy NEC 840A (Navy Scuba Diver)
      • Navy NEC O50A (Special Warfare Boat Operator (SB) Candidate)
      • Navy NEC O52A (Special Warfare Combatant-craft Crewman (SWCC))
      • Navy NEC G02A (Helicopter Search and Rescue Aircrew Swimmer)
      • Navy NEC 806A (Aviation Water Survival Instructor)
      • Navy NEC 808A (Basic Swimming and Water Survival Instructor)
      • USMC MOS 0918 (Water Safety/Survival Instructor)
  • Possess current certification in Tier 2 Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) (or TCCC Instructor/Trainer certification)
  • Possess current certification in Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)
  • Possess current certification as a CPR Instructor Certification
Minimum Education

  • High school diploma or GED required.
